items.title: Are passwords protected by adaptive hashing?
items.description: Password and reset flows must use reviewed adaptive hashing parameters.
items.verification: Inspect every bcrypt.hash call in registration, reset, change-password and OAuth bootstrap; test correct and incorrect passwords.
items.remediation: Centralize the password cost policy and migrate weak hashes on successful authentication.

items.title: Are token expiry, rotation and revocation enforced?
items.description: Server sessions must expire and reject revoked tokens, including concurrent refresh attempts.
items.verification: Run npm --prefix server run test:invariants; exercise expired, revoked and replayed refresh credentials.
items.remediation: Enforce server expiry and session epochs; persist rotated credentials atomically.

items.title: Are login and recovery attempts rate-limited across replicas?
items.description: Distributed limits must bound guessing without exposing account existence.
items.verification: Send repeated invalid logins and resets against two replicas; record rejection thresholds and Redis outage behavior.
items.remediation: Use shared rate limits and generic account recovery responses.

items.title: Does every protected operation deny unauthenticated requests?
items.description: Authentication hydration alone does not protect routes; each protected operation needs an enforcement gate.
items.verification: Run middleware-coverage and requireOnboarded-bypass server tests; call changed routes with missing and malformed credentials.
items.remediation: Attach required authentication and onboarding gates before handlers.

items.title: Are role, ownership and plan checks enforced by the server?
items.description: Persisted authority controls admin, organization and team operations. Hidden UI is not authorization.
items.verification: Attempt each changed privileged action as fan, unrelated coach and non-owner; assert denial and no write.
items.remediation: Resolve authority from persisted membership and shared server policy.

items.title: Do sensitive operations require appropriate reauthentication?
items.description: Document the threat-based MFA or recent-authentication requirement for admin, credential and deletion operations.
items.verification: Exercise stale sessions on sensitive actions; attach evidence of reauthentication or an explicit reviewed gap.
items.remediation: Require recent authentication or MFA appropriate to the operation; track unsupported controls as unresolved.

items.title: Is third-party identity verified before account linking?
items.description: Provider identity, audience and ownership must be verified before linking an account.
items.verification: Run npm --prefix server run test:invariants and negative tests for wrong audience, issuer and existing linked accounts.
items.remediation: Verify provider assertions server-side and reject ambiguous ownership.

items.title: Do frontend and backend validation contracts agree?
items.description: Backend validation is authoritative; intentional UX differences need explicit documentation.
items.verification: Compare apiclient schemas and changed forms against server schemas; run validation-consistency and validation-parity tests.
items.remediation: Share safe schemas or add parity cases for boundaries and malformed values.

items.title: Are all external inputs validated server-side?
items.description: Validate body, path, query and asynchronous provider inputs before effects.
items.verification: Submit missing, wrong-type, oversized and unknown fields to changed endpoints; assert safe rejection.
items.remediation: Parse allowlisted schemas before database access or side effects.

items.title: Can only trusted server logic set critical state?
items.description: Payment, approval, ownership, plan and privileged role fields cannot be client-authored.
items.verification: Submit protected fields through create, update and onboarding routes; compare persisted state before and after.
items.remediation: Allowlist mutable fields and derive privileged state from trusted records.

items.title: Are database and command operations injection-safe?
items.description: Parameterized access must cover raw queries and dynamic identifiers as well as ordinary Prisma calls.
items.verification: Review raw SQL and subprocess call sites; probe attacker-controlled strings and identifier allowlists.
items.remediation: Parameterize values and explicitly allowlist identifiers; avoid shell interpolation.

items.title: Is untrusted content safely rendered?
items.description: Public HTML and web surfaces must encode user content and use suitable response security policies.
items.verification: Insert HTML payloads in rendered fields; inspect public route responses and production CSP without executing untrusted scripts.
items.remediation: Escape output by context and restrict unsafe markup and scripts.

items.title: Are uploads checked before they become accessible?
items.description: Validate actual media type, size, ownership and scanning or moderation policy; client metadata is untrusted.
items.verification: Upload disallowed, oversized and mismatched-content fixtures; confirm denial and inaccessible rejected objects.
items.remediation: Enforce server media validation and quarantine or reject unverified objects.

items.title: Are request size and collection limits bounded?
items.description: Bound payloads, pagination and batch operations before expensive processing.
items.verification: Inspect server parser limits and submit oversized JSON, uploads and pagination values; record safe failures.
items.remediation: Apply parser limits, bounded page sizes and workload-specific rate limits.

items.title: Do privacy, blocking and minor-safety rules fail closed?
items.description: Age, consent, blocking and private resource policies must apply to reads, writes and media access.
items.verification: Exercise adult/minor, blocked-user and private-team combinations; verify denied messages and no hidden data in responses.
items.remediation: Reuse server privacy and age policies for every access path.

items.title: Are secrets absent from client bundles and logs?
items.description: Public Expo configuration must never contain private provider or database credentials.
items.verification: Run the secret-scan workflow; inspect production bundle/config and redacted logs using synthetic secrets.
items.remediation: Remove exposed values, rotate affected credentials and load secrets only on trusted servers.

items.title: Are keys and credentials rotated with an owner?
items.description: Rotation must cover database, signing and provider credentials with a tested transition.
items.verification: Attach redacted rotation records, owner and next due date; exercise old-key rejection in a safe environment.
items.remediation: Document rotation ownership and overlapping key rollout where needed.

items.title: Is transport encrypted across every trust boundary?
items.description: Verify HTTPS for public traffic and TLS for database, Redis and provider connections.
items.verification: Inspect deployed redirects, TLS and connection settings; confirm cleartext requests cannot transmit credentials.
items.remediation: Require TLS and verify certificates; document edge proxy enforcement.

items.title: Is sensitive persisted data encrypted and access-restricted?
items.description: Database, object storage and backups need verified encryption and least-privilege access.
items.verification: Attach redacted provider encryption settings and access review; verify backup encryption configuration.
items.remediation: Enable encryption with controlled key access and restrict data roles.

items.title: Are session credentials stored safely on each platform?
items.description: Native credentials require SecureStore; browser credential persistence needs a separately reviewed threat model.
items.verification: Inspect native and web branches in auth storage and test storage failure and reinstall recovery.
items.remediation: Keep native tokens in secure storage; remove unsafe browser persistence and fail closed on storage errors.

items.title: Are provider signatures verified before effects?
items.description: Webhook and purchase claims require authentic signatures, expected identity and fresh timestamp policy.
items.verification: Submit missing, invalid and wrong-provider signatures; verify zero writes and inspect raw-body handling.
items.remediation: Use provider verification with expected application identity before processing callbacks.

items.title: Is cross-origin access limited to intended clients?
items.description: CORS policy must specify trusted browser origins without treating CORS as authentication.
items.verification: Test allowed and untrusted Origin headers, including preflight and credentialed requests.
items.remediation: Use an explicit environment-specific origin allowlist.

items.title: Does resource access check actor-to-object authorization?
items.description: Valid IDs must not allow access to another user’s private objects or operations.
items.verification: Swap resource IDs between two unrelated accounts for read, write, delete and export; assert denied access.
items.remediation: Scope queries and mutations to authorized owners or members.

items.title: Are retries and webhook replays duplicate-safe?
items.description: Repeated and out-of-order callbacks must preserve one correct final state across replicas.
items.verification: Run npm --prefix server run test:payments:confidence; replay the same event concurrently and assert one entitlement/write.
items.remediation: Use durable event identifiers, transactions and shared locks instead of in-process dedupe.

items.title: Is paid state confirmed independently by the server?
items.description: Success URLs, local purchase state and client payloads cannot grant entitlements.
items.verification: Forge success/deep-link parameters and receipt payloads; verify no paid state until provider verification succeeds.
items.remediation: Reconcile payment state from verified provider data and return authoritative status.

items.title: Are error responses sanitized and actionable?
items.description: Responses must omit secrets, stack traces and internal paths while retaining safe diagnostic references.
items.verification: Trigger validation, authorization and server errors; inspect responses and correlated redacted logs.
items.remediation: Centralize safe error formatting with correlation identifiers.

items.title: Are API contract changes compatible with supported clients?
items.description: Mobile releases may lag the server; version or migrate breaking request and response changes.
items.verification: Compare changed schemas to previous supported clients and run contract fixtures; record compatibility window.
items.remediation: Use additive changes or explicit versioned migration with deprecation dates.

items.title: Do routes delegate shared policy and networking?
items.description: Keep routing wrappers small and reusable policy in shared modules; clients use apiclient transport.
items.verification: Review changed app wrappers and raw fetch calls; document approved transport exceptions with reasons.
items.remediation: Move duplicate policy into shared helpers and network calls into apiclient.

items.title: Do deep links resolve safely with validated parameters?
items.description: Email, push and OAuth navigation must handle malformed routes without privileged side effects.
items.verification: Run deepLinks-navigation and route-integrity tests; open missing, malformed and unauthorized parameters.
items.remediation: Validate target and parameters and use safe public fallbacks.

items.title: Are dependency vulnerabilities reviewed before release?
items.description: Scan app, server and audit-tool dependencies; findings need exploitability assessment and ownership.
items.verification: Run npm audit in each package and inspect security workflow results; record unresolved advisories.
items.remediation: Upgrade vulnerable dependencies or record a scoped reviewed exception with expiry.

items.title: Are production bundles built and inspected?
items.description: Release artifacts must use production settings and avoid debug endpoints or secret-bearing source maps.
items.verification: Build the intended release target; inspect resulting config, minification and source-map access.
items.remediation: Use release profiles and restrict debug tooling and source-map distribution.

items.title: Do asynchronous screens show loading, empty, success and error states?
items.description: Users need clear recovery without duplicate submissions or stale effects after unmount.
items.verification: Exercise slow, failed and empty responses, double submissions and navigation during requests.
items.remediation: Add explicit state handling, submission guards and cancellation or mounted checks.

items.title: Are critical controls usable with keyboard and assistive technology?
items.description: Names, focus, text status and adequate targets must communicate actions without color alone.
items.verification: Use keyboard and screen reader on login, payments and audit flows; inspect focus and announced statuses.
items.remediation: Add accessible labels, visible focus and text status; restore focus after transitions.

items.title: Is persisted client state limited and isolated by identity?
items.description: Feature-local progress can persist locally; sensitive authority and previous-user data cannot be trusted.
items.verification: Switch accounts and corrupt or exhaust storage; verify reset, validation and a visible recovery path.
items.remediation: Validate stored data, scope caches by account and keep security decisions server-owned.

items.title: Does CI use least-privilege credentials and permissions?
items.description: Untrusted pull requests must not access deployment secrets or privileged write tokens.
items.verification: Review workflow triggers, permissions, pinned actions and fork behavior; attach the relevant run URL.
items.remediation: Separate untrusted checks from deployments and minimize job permissions.

items.title: Are database credentials restricted and externally managed?
items.description: Runtime credentials should have only needed privileges and stay out of tracked configuration.
items.verification: Inspect redacted deployment bindings and database role grants; verify repository secret scan.
items.remediation: Use secret-managed credentials, restricted roles and rotation.

items.title: Are public and internal network surfaces restricted?
items.description: Confirm ingress, database exposure and WAF or equivalent abuse controls against deployment evidence.
items.verification: Attach firewall/edge policy evidence and test denied access to internal services from an external network.
items.remediation: Restrict service ingress and configure abuse protections for exposed endpoints.

items.title: Can encrypted backups be restored successfully?
items.description: Backup success alone does not demonstrate recovery of schema and usable data.
items.verification: Review a recent backup-restore-drill run and record restore duration, integrity checks and recovery objectives.
items.remediation: Automate isolated restore drills and address integrity or recovery-time failures.

items.title: Is deployment configuration versioned and reviewed?
items.description: Runtime, build and environment changes require review and reproducible configuration.
items.verification: Compare deployed settings to versioned configuration; record any provider-only settings and owner.
items.remediation: Version non-secret configuration and document external setting changes.

items.title: Are migrations and rollout changes reversible?
items.description: Record deployment order, compatibility, rollback triggers and feature flags for risky changes.
items.verification: Exercise migration and rollback in staging; attach migration status and a tested recovery procedure.
items.remediation: Use compatible migrations and staged rollout with explicit rollback ownership.

items.title: Is cross-replica coordination durable?
items.description: Locks, dedupe and rate limits need shared state and defined outage behavior.
items.verification: Run concurrent operations on two replicas and simulate shared-store loss; assert no duplicate critical effects.
items.remediation: Use Redis or database coordination with bounded locks and safe failure handling.

items.title: Are security-relevant failures observable?
items.description: Auth failures, validation rejection and blocked privileged actions need useful redacted telemetry.
items.verification: Trigger synthetic failures and find their timestamp, action and correlation ID in collected logs.
items.remediation: Emit structured security events without tokens or unnecessary personal data.

items.title: Do sensitive admin actions leave authoritative audit evidence?
items.description: Audit records must identify actor, target, action, timestamp and outcome for privileged mutations.
items.verification: Trace each changed admin mutation and confirm a durable audit record for success and meaningful failure paths.
items.remediation: Write durable audit records through shared logging at the mutation boundary.

items.title: Are logs and error telemetry scrubbed of sensitive data?
items.description: Passwords, tokens, payment details and unnecessary minor data must not enter telemetry.
items.verification: Send synthetic canary secrets through error paths and inspect logs and Sentry payloads for redaction.
items.remediation: Apply shared recursive redaction before every telemetry sink.

items.title: Do anomaly alerts reach an accountable responder?
items.description: Auth spikes, payment failures and job failures need actionable thresholds and routing.
items.verification: Trigger a safe test alert and record receipt, owner and linked response procedure.
items.remediation: Configure signal-specific thresholds and test delivery to the on-call owner.

items.title: Is the incident response procedure executable?
items.description: The runbook must identify triage, containment, recovery, communication and ownership.
items.verification: Run a tabletop auth or payment incident and document missing access, steps and follow-up owners.
items.remediation: Maintain tested response steps and current escalation ownership.

items.title: Is security-log retention defined and verified?
items.description: Verify the requested 90-day security retention target against minimization and access policy.
items.verification: Attach configured retention evidence and an old-event retrieval test; record approved deviations explicitly.
items.remediation: Set documented retention, access and deletion policies with reviewed exceptions.

items.title: Does every finding and pass have reproducible evidence?
items.description: A checked box or successful source scan cannot establish behavioral security. Unknown controls remain unresolved.
items.verification: Attach commit, environment, command/test, result and timestamp for every passed item; require proof and notes for failures.
items.remediation: Record before/after reproduction and explicit manual-review evidence.

items.title: Are slow database operations measured?
items.description: Collect representative latency and query behavior for critical endpoints without logging sensitive values.
items.verification: Capture staging query timing and endpoint percentiles under representative load; compare to stated budgets.
items.remediation: Instrument slow queries and optimize measured bottlenecks.

items.title: Do cache invalidations preserve privacy and current authority?
items.description: Account, block, approval and payment transitions must invalidate affected cache entries.
items.verification: Run games-cache-invalidation, users-follow-cache-invalidation and auth-me-cache-invalidation server tests; verify changed flows.
items.remediation: Invalidate or version affected caches and recheck authorization on sensitive reads.

items.title: Are asset caches efficient and privacy-safe?
items.description: Cache public immutable media appropriately while preventing shared caches from leaking private responses.
items.verification: Inspect CDN and API Cache-Control behavior for public assets and authenticated content after logout.
items.remediation: Set explicit public/private cache policy and version immutable asset URLs.

items.title: Are expensive screens and assets loaded on demand?
items.description: Measure route startup and defer nonessential work while keeping loading and error states accessible.
items.verification: Profile a production build on a representative device and inspect eager imports on primary routes.
items.remediation: Defer heavy optional modules and media based on measured startup cost.

items.title: Is delivered bundle size within an explicit budget?
items.description: Track compressed web assets and native release size separately; the audit page targets less than 3 MB gzip.
items.verification: Build tools/audit and measure total delivered compressed assets; compare app build artifacts to recorded budgets.
items.remediation: Remove unused dependencies, split expensive modules and record approved budget changes.

items.title: Are list endpoints bounded and free of avoidable N+1 queries?
items.description: Query count and memory should remain bounded as lists grow.
items.verification: Measure query counts at page sizes 1, 10 and the maximum; verify indexed filters and pagination.
items.remediation: Batch related lookups, use suitable indexes and enforce pagination.
